ownerDecisions.summary: Upstream component set from sealed files: official v1.37.1 apiserver, controller-manager, scheduler, kubelet and kube-proxy (nftables); etcd on a unix socket; containerd 2.x and runc (cgroupfs); CNI bridge, host-local and loopback; kube-network-policies (nftables); no CoreDNS.

License closure of the release binaries (statically linked glibc, libseccomp, libpathrs; host nft): L-a reviewed policy entries with the official binaries, L-b dynamic builds, L-c an Apache-only closure.
etcd line: E-a v3.7.2 (Kubernetes v1.37.1 is built and tested with 3.7), E-b v3.6.15.
kube-network-policies publishes images only: N-a build the standard command from the tag, N-b take the binary from the release image pinned by digest.

parts.name: cni-plugins
excludedMembers: every plugin other than bridge, host-local and loopback

notes: containerd 2.4 is listed for Kubernetes 1.37 in containerd's RELEASES.md matrix (2.4.0+, 2.3.0+, CRI v1).

containerd starts containerd-shim-runc-v2, which daemonizes and is reparented away from containerd; runc and the container processes are the shim's children. containerd executes the CNI plugins (bridge, host-local IPAM, loopback) for pod networking on one node. runc uses the cgroupfs driver (SystemdCgroup false).

Sealed containerd configuration: the gRPC socket at /run/qualification-k8s/containerd.sock (with its .ttrpc companion), NRI disabled ([plugins."io.containerd.nri.v1.nri"] disable = true), the debug socket unset, the sandbox image pinned by digest, no registry mirrors.

The static archive links glibc statically (CGO_ENABLED=1 with -extldflags -static; only the shim is built with cgo off); runc's static release links glibc, libseccomp 2.6.1 and libpathrs 0.2.6 (review entries).

Owner decision Q-E: etcd v3.7.2. Kubernetes v1.37.1 builds and tests against etcd 3.7.0 (build/dependencies.yaml:66-67; kubeadm DefaultEtcdVersion 3.7.0-0); 3.6 remains supported (MinExternalEtcdVersion 3.5.24-0).

cmd/kube-network-policies/standard at a145b01c, GOOS=linux GOARCH=arm64 CGO_ENABLED=0, pinned Go toolchain and module cache (D-NETPOL-BUILD)

notes: The project publishes container images only, no release binaries (owner question Q-N); the standard command enforces NetworkPolicy through netlink nftables (github.com/google/nftables, no nft binary) and uses no CustomResourceDefinitions.

Sealed flags: --fail-open=false (the default true leaves traffic unenforced while the agent is down), --disable-nri, a loopback --metrics-bind-address (the default :9080 listens on every interface), --kubeconfig with its closure identity, --hostname-override with the node name.
Runs in nftables mode (--proxy-mode=nftables), which executes the host's nft, version 1.0.1 or later (vendor/sigs.k8s.io/knftables/nftables.go:152,162-163); healthz and metrics bind loopback.

criteria.how: I06 v2 evidence binds one W02a v3 record by digest. No production W02a backend profile exists yet (the unit-distribution fixture is test-only), so this selection cannot yield evidence on its own: W02a-F2 adds the production profile that names these components and W02g-F2 binds an I06 successor to it (I06 v2 R1-4).

etcd v3.7.2 as one member, with no TCP listener. Client: --listen-client-urls unix:///run/qualification-k8s/datastore.sock (a unix client listener uses the URL's host and path, server/embed/etcd.go:750-753). etcd cannot run without a peer listener: --listen-peer-urls="" is accepted as the flag's empty-string exception (server/embed/config.go:608-609, pkg/flags/unique_urls.go Set) and leaves the default http://localhost:2380 (config.go:87) in place, so the peer listener is one AF_UNIX socket. The peer listener passes only the URL's host to the listener (server/embed/etcd.go:576), so its form is unix://<name>:<port>, a socket file relative to etcd's working directory, which is the datastore's private directory (unix:///<absolute path> would name an autobound abstract socket). --initial-advertise-peer-urls and --advertise-client-urls must be host:port forms (checkHostURLs, config.go:961-965), and the latter is required once --listen-client-urls is set (server/etcdmain/config.go:251); both are advertisement values with no listener. I06 v1 and v2 require peerListen == [], which etcd cannot meet (D-SC01-PEER).

kube-apiserver --bind-address=127.0.0.1 with the I06 v2 positive evidence's secure port; the kubelet, kube-proxy and the policy agent reach it through loopback kubeconfigs. The other components' listeners, which default to every interface, are pinned to loopback too: kube-controller-manager and kube-scheduler --bind-address=127.0.0.1, kube-proxy healthz and metrics on 127.0.0.1.

kube-apiserver: --anonymous-auth=false; no --token-auth-file; bootstrap-token authentication off (default); no --requestheader-* flags; no --authentication-config, OIDC or webhook authenticator; --service-account-signing-key-file readable only by the apiserver's domain, --service-account-key-file its public half only, one --service-account-issuer, --service-account-lookup=true. kube-controller-manager has no --cluster-signing-* or --service-account-private-key-file. Client certificates come from the off-host CA (W01 P4), so no CA key is on the host.

kube-apiserver --authorization-config pointing at a sealed structured file whose authorizers are Node then RBAC; v1.37.1 reloads the file on change (upstream facts, authorizationConfig), and only maintenance can write a sealed type.

--enable-admission-plugins and --disable-admission-plugins give exactly the I06 v2 allowed set: NodeRestriction on; webhook admission, MutatingAdmissionPolicy, NamespaceAutoProvision, ImagePolicyWebhook and AlwaysAdmit off. --admission-control-config-file carries the manifest-based admission configuration (OR08).

kube-controller-manager --use-service-account-credentials=true and --controllers naming exactly the I06 v2 positive evidence's 34 controllers, a subset of the 49-controller inventory in which the ten required-disabled controllers are off (CSR signing, approving and cleaner, bootstrap signer, token cleaner, legacy token controller and cleaner, ClusterRole aggregation, storage-version migrator, ClusterTrustBundle publisher); no signing key file.

KubeletConfiguration: rotateCertificates false, serverTLSBootstrap false, no staticPodPath or staticPodURL, authentication.anonymous.enabled false, readOnlyPort 0, authorization.mode Webhook; no --bootstrap-kubeconfig.

Eight component processes from distinct upstream executables: etcd, kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, kubelet, containerd, kube-proxy and kube-network-policies. No multi-call binary. CONTAINER_RUNTIME also spans helper executables: containerd-shim-runc-v2 (which daemonizes away from containerd), runc and the container processes under the shim, and the CNI plugins that containerd executes; kube-proxy executes the host's nft. The five Kubernetes binaries have distinct published digests per architecture; etcd's and containerd's digests cover their archives, and the agent's digest is recorded at build. Canonical paths, the confined types of components and helpers and their verity digests come from the production W02a profile (D-W02A-F2, D-HELPER-TYPES).

No selected component registers a CustomResourceDefinition or an aggregated APIService: kube-network-policies runs only its standard command (its npa-v1alpha1 and npa-v1alpha2 commands, which use AdminNetworkPolicy CRDs, are not built), kube-proxy and the CNI plugins use none, and no metrics-server is selected. The observer still refuses either at runtime.

Every backend component is a host process, so no backend Pod mounts a token. The only component API clients are kube-proxy (system:kube-proxy) and kube-network-policies, each with its closure identity in a sealed kubeconfig holding an off-host-issued client certificate.

Every containerd listener is closed to all but the kubelet: the gRPC socket /run/qualification-k8s/containerd.sock (the I06 v2 positive evidence's path) and its .ttrpc companion carry a type that only the kubelet's confined type may connect to (W02e matrix); NRI, on by default in containerd 2.4 (/var/run/nri/nri.sock, external connections allowed), is disabled in the sealed configuration and the policy agent runs with --disable-nri; the debug socket stays unset. No other CRI client is installed: ctr and containerd-stress are left out of the archive.

The sealed set is the I06 v2 positive evidence's files: ADMISSION_CONFIG, APISERVER_FLAGS, AUTHORIZATION_CONFIG, CNI_CONFIG (one conflist: bridge, host-local, loopback), COMPONENT_DEFINITIONS, CONTAINER_RUNTIME_CONFIG, CONTROLLER_MANAGER_FLAGS, DATASTORE_CONFIG, ENCRYPTION_CONFIG (kube-apiserver --encryption-provider-config), KUBECONFIGS, KUBELET_CONFIG, NETWORK_POLICY_AGENT_CONFIG, PKI_TRUST_BUNDLES, SCHEDULER_FLAGS and SERVICE_PROXY_CONFIG, plus the conditional files when used (admission manifests for OR08, an audit policy); no static pod or auto-apply manifest directory. Exact paths come with the host-image packet.

Every artifact is pinned by the upstream's published SHA-256 (Kubernetes .sha256 files on dl.k8s.io, etcd SHA256SUMS, containerd and CNI checksum files, runc.sha256sum), the source-built agent by commit and the sandbox image by index digest. Installation is from the host image only; no component updates itself; images, including the sandbox image, are imported into containerd's content store at enrollment with no registry reachable. Every upstream project is Apache-2.0, but the release binaries are not Apache-only: runc, containerd's static archive and the pause binary link glibc statically, runc also links libseccomp and libpathrs, and kube-proxy executes the host's nft (license reviews decided by owner question Q-L). I06's SC13 model admits only distribution.license == Apache-2.0 (D-I06-LICENSE).

The five Kubernetes executables are the official v1.37.1 release builds of tag commit f78e7223, which report gitVersion v1.37.1 with no vendor suffix (I06 N5); the evidence record's kubernetesVersion confirms it at enrollment.
No --feature-gates, --emulated-version, --min-compatibility-version or --runtime-config flag or configuration field in any Kubernetes component, so every gate keeps its v1.37 default.

The closure (identity-closure.json) was derived from v1.37.1 bootstrap RBAC, which the selected apiserver runs; the planeon identities get client certificates with their fixed names from the off-host CA; check_closure runs against the observer's snapshot.
Checked by check_rbac_snapshot on every observer snapshot.
Checked by check_rbac_snapshot on every observer snapshot.
Checked by check_rbac_snapshot; the observer also refuses to produce a snapshot when a non-resource-URL rule is bound to system:apiserver (I06 v2 R1-7, a W03 observer obligation).
Checked by check_rbac_snapshot on every observer snapshot.
Checked by check_rbac_snapshot on every observer snapshot.

Unchanged for the upstream apiserver: a restart during ACTIVE invalidates the generation, because bootstrap-roles and the system-namespace and authentication-info controllers write policy kinds at start.
Policy-kind objects carry no ownerReferences, so the upstream garbage collector cannot delete them; observer-checked.
The aggregation controller is off (SC06), so no ClusterRole with an aggregationRule may be bound in the qualification namespace; observer-checked.
API Priority and Fairness objects affect availability only; system:masters is exempt; only the in-process producer writes them.
The legacy token controller is off (SC06) and bootstrap tokens are unused (SC03), so no service-account-token or bootstrap-token Secret exists; observer-checked.
No webhook configuration or MutatingAdmissionPolicy object exists although their plugins are off; observer-checked.
The observer starts INSPECTING only after /readyz/poststarthook/rbac/bootstrap-roles succeeds on the apiserver.

The A2 admission policies are held in sealed manifest-based admission files (ManifestBasedAdmissionControlConfig, beta and on by default in v1.37.1, so no feature gate changes; admission semantics v3).

excluded.candidate: k3s, k0s, RKE2 and other single-binary or repackaged distributions
excluded.reason: One multi-call executable for several components, or a vendor-suffixed version.
Kubernetes does not build or test against its emulated etcd API; its SQLite backend needs CGO and the SQLite blessing is not a classified license; embedded, it is not a separate process.

excluded.candidate: kubeadm (as installer or for its defaults)
excluded.reason: Its defaults enable bootstrap tokens and CSR signing; the profile is built from sealed files with no installer.
CustomResourceDefinitions (SC09); their BPF datapaths also exceed W02e E1's cgroup-device-only rule.
Not needed by the qualification workloads (owner decision Q4).
GPL-2.0-or-later is not in the license policy's allowed or review lists.
Clients, not components; left out of the installed set.

licenseReviews.subject: glibc statically linked into containerd (static archive), runc and the pause binary
licenseReviews.reason: containerd's release builds with CGO and -extldflags -static (Makefile:96-108, 332-336); runc's make static links static-pie against a Debian glibc toolchain; kubernetes build/pause compiles -static.

licenseReviews.subject: libseccomp 2.6.1 statically linked into runc
licenseReviews.reason: runc's BUILDTAGS include seccomp; the release ships libseccomp-2.6.1.tar.gz for compliance.

licenseReviews.subject: libpathrs 0.2.6 and its Rust crate closure statically linked into runc
licenseReviews.reason: runc's BUILDTAGS include libpathrs; the release ships libpathrs-0.2.6.tar.xz; the dual expression is not an allowed exception under exact matching.

licenseReviews.subject: nft, executed by kube-proxy from the host image
licenseReviews.reason: A separately executed host program; GPL-2.0-only is on the policy's explicit-review list.

openItems.text: A production W02a backend profile with these components' canonical paths, confined types and verity digests, and an I06 successor bound to it, before any evidence record.

etcd cannot run without a peer listener, so the I06 successor accepts exactly one AF_UNIX peer listener, unix://<name>:<port> relative to etcd's working directory (the datastore's private directory), reachable only from the datastore's confined type, and no TCP listener; native evidence shows no TCP listener. I06's unix:///<absolute path> convention cannot express etcd's peer socket.
Map the helper executables (containerd-shim-runc-v2, runc, the CNI plugins, the host's nft) to confined types under I06's one-entry-type-per-domain rule.

Owner decision Q-L (L-a): amend legal/third-party-license-policy.yaml with a reviewed class for host-OS and statically linked system libraries holding exactly LGPL-2.1-or-later (glibc), LGPL-2.1-only (libseccomp), MPL-2.0 OR LGPL-3.0-or-later electing MPL-2.0 (libpathrs) and GPL-2.0-only for separately executed host programs (nft), with source offers from the pinned tags. Validators pin the policy identity (validate_reuse: policyVersion 0.3.0), so the amendment is its own history-projected packet before the host-image packet.
Replace I06 SC13's single distribution.license == Apache-2.0 check with a reference to the reviewed license closure, once owner question Q-L is decided.

License closure and SBOM of every artifact: Go module sets, the statically linked C and Rust libraries (D-LIC-GLIBC, D-LIC-LIBSECCOMP, D-LIC-LIBPATHRS), and host runtime dependencies (nft 1.0.1 or later, D-LIC-NFT), against legal/third-party-license-policy.yaml.
Build kube-network-policies cmd/kube-network-policies/standard at a145b01c for both architectures with a pinned Go toolchain and module cache, CGO off, and record the digests (owner question Q-N).
Pin containerd's sandbox image to registry.k8s.io/pause:3.10.2 by index digest and import it at enrollment.
Confirm on the enrolled kernel that containerd and runc load only cgroup-device programs under the cgroupfs driver (W02e E1) and that the CNI plugins and kube-proxy in nftables mode load none.
